chunks: From him, from Salamah, from Ali ibn al-Mundhir al-Zabbal, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you have a dirham, buy wheat with it, for the deficiency (in weight/measure) is in the flour.

key_terms.الْمَحْق: Deficiency, shrinkage, or loss in measure/weight
key_terms.دِرْهَمٌ: A silver coin used as currency

ai.seo_question: Why is it better to buy wheat than flour according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of *al-Talqqi* (speculative buying) and *al-Hukrah* (monopoly/hoarding) in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the economic prudence of avoiding processed goods prone to hidden deficiency (*maḥq*). By advising the purchase of raw wheat over flour, the Imam (peace be upon him) underscores the importance of preserving the intrinsic value and weight of commodities against the shrinkage caused by moisture loss or settling, a key concern in Shia commercial jurisprudence.
